title: Microaxial Flow Pump Use and Renal Outcomes in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Secondary Analysis of the DanGer Shock Trial
summary: This prespecified secondary analysis of DanGer Shock included 355 adults randomized to Impella CP plus standard care or standard care alone for STEMI-related cardiogenic shock. AKI occurred in 61% versus 45%, and renal replacement therapy in 42% versus 27%; the dialysis excess persisted after accounting for death as a competing event (subdistribution hazard ratio 1.67, 95% CI 1.18–2.35). Survivors were dialysis-free at 180 days, which does not establish normal long-term kidney function.
findings: Death-competing-risk analysis: RRT subdistribution hazard ratio 1.67 (95% CI 1.18–2.35).
No dialysis among 180-day survivors; serum creatinine was not measured at that time.
population: Adults with STEMI-related cardiogenic shock in Denmark, Germany and the United Kingdom; comatose out-of-hospital arrest, right ventricular failure and septic shock were excluded.
shortTitle: DanGer Shock: greater kidney injury and dialysis with microaxial support
limitations: RRT initiation was unblinded and clinician-directed; baseline dialysis status was not recorded, and 180-day creatinine was unavailable. The trial excluded several high-risk shock presentations. Nonprespecified mediation and postrandomization AKI subgroups are vulnerable to survivor bias and cannot establish preserved causal survival benefit despite kidney injury.
intervention: Impella CP microaxial flow pump plus standard care (179 participants).
whyItMatters: When discussing mechanical support with the shock team, weigh this renal harm alongside the parent trial’s survival findings and plan close renal, bleeding and device surveillance; these data do not justify routine use across all shock phenotypes.
